group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 28-year-old man who works as a warehouse inventory clerk and lives with two roommates in a third-floor walk-up apartment arrived at the emergency department around 09:30 after waking with shaking chills, pleuritic right-sided chest discomfort, and another fever spike that he measured at home as “just over 39 °C”; wanting the clinical staff to see his baseline physiology, he took no acetaminophen, used no inhalers, and declined the albuterol nebulizer occasionally prescribed for exertional wheeze during the 45-minute ride his co-worker provided. His past medical background includes a non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy diagnosed six years ago following a viral prodrome, most recent outpatient echocardiogram documenting a left-ventricular ejection fraction of 25 % with mild functional mitral regurgitation and stable biventricular dimensions; carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily and sacubitril-valsartan 49/51 mg twice daily are taken routinely, although he admits missing yesterday evening’s dose because of nausea. Three years ago he progressed to end-stage kidney failure from biopsy-proven focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and has since been maintained on automated peritoneal dialysis overnight; his nephrologist typically records predialysis urea nitrogen in the high 60s with creatinine near 10 mg/dL and advises a fluid limit of 1.0 L per day plus a strict low-sodium diet, which the patient concedes he broke during a weekend barbecue “because the wings were salty.” He has never experienced transient ischemic attack, stroke, or any malignancy, and apart from occasional loop diuretic use for lower-extremity swelling he takes no additional prescription drugs. He quit smoking e-cigarettes two years ago, drinks beer socially once or twice a month, denies illicit substance use, and received the current season’s influenza vaccine at a pharmacy in October along with a 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide booster during a dialysis visit. On roll-in he sat upright on the stretcher, speaking in full sentences, oriented to date, location, and situation, and able to recall three objects at five minutes. Skin was flushed and lightly diaphoretic but capillary refill remained under two seconds; jugular venous pulsation was visualized to about 4 cm above the sternal angle at 45°, consistent with prior cardiology notes, and trace ankle edema was present. Untreated triage vitals were: tympanic temperature 38.95 °C, regular yet pronounced tachycardia at 143 beats min⁻¹ confirmed on telemetry, automated blood pressure 153/88 mm Hg corroborated manually, respirations 28 breaths min⁻¹ with moderate depth but no accessory muscle use, and fingertip pulse oximetry 97 % while breathing ambient air at sea-level altitude. Cardiac auscultation revealed a rapid S1/S2 with a soft third heart sound but no new murmurs or pericardial rub. Pulmonary examination demonstrated diminished breath sounds and coarse crackles over the posterior right lower lung field with dullness to percussion extending halfway up the scapular tip; the left lung was clear and resonant. The abdomen was soft with a well-healed peri-umbilical Tenckhoff catheter tunnel site, no organomegaly, and normal bowel sounds. Neurologic screen showed equal, reactive pupils, intact extra-ocular movements, fluent speech, and symmetric 5/5 strength throughout. Finger-stick glucose obtained before vascular access measured 106 mg/dL. Venous chemistry drawn within ten minutes of arrival—prior to any intravenous fluids or heparinized saline flushes—returned sodium 171 mEq/L, potassium 4.3 mEq/L, chloride 121 mEq/L, bicarbonate 19 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 74 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 9.8 mg/dL, values consistent with his usual predialysis range except for a higher than typical sodium attributed to dietary indiscretion and volume depletion. Complete blood count revealed leukocytes 15.2 × 10⁹/L with 86 % segmented neutrophils, hematocrit 48 %, hemoglobin 16.0 g/dL, and platelets 235 × 10⁹/L. A right radial arterial sample obtained as he continued on room air demonstrated a marked alkalemia with pH 7.72, PaCO₂ 24 mm Hg, PaO₂ 105 mm Hg, and calculated bicarbonate 26 mEq/L, consistent with a primary respiratory alkalosis likely driven by fever and tachypnea. Serum lactate was 1.7 mmol/L. A portable postero-anterior chest radiograph completed before any treatment displayed a dense consolidation in the right lower lobe with air bronchograms and a small meniscus-shaped opacity layering laterally along the same hemithorax, compatible with a reactive pleural fluid collection; cardiac silhouette appeared mildly enlarged, unchanged from a film six months earlier. Electrocardiography showed sinus tachycardia at 142 beats min⁻¹ with nonspecific ST-T changes but no new ischemic pattern compared with his baseline tracing. Two sets of peripheral blood cultures, an induced sputum specimen for Gram stain and culture, urinary antigens for Streptococcus pneumoniae and Legionella, and a multiplex respiratory viral panel were dispatched before initiation of antimicrobials, antipyretics, intravenous crystalloids, bronchodilators, dialysis, or supplemental oxygen, ensuring that all physiologic observations, laboratory values, and imaging findings documented above reflect the patient’s condition prior to any hospital intervention.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) uses demographics, comorbidities, and pretreatment findings.
- Demographics: a 28-year-old man starts at 28 points. He lives at home, so the nursing-home adjustment is 0.
- Comorbidities: heart failure with EF 25% (+10) and dialysis-dependent renal disease (+10). No documented malignancy, liver disease, or cerebrovascular disease (0 each).
- Examination: pulse 143/min meets the ≥125 threshold (+10). He is oriented, respiratory rate 28 is <30/min, systolic pressure 153 is ≥90 mmHg, and temperature 38.95°C is neither <35 nor ≥40°C (0 each).
- Tests: BUN 74 mg/dL is ≥30 (+20), and the radiograph shows a pleural effusion (+10). Arterial pH 7.72 is not <7.35; sodium 171 is not <130 mEq/L; glucose 106 is not ≥250 mg/dL; hematocrit 48% is not <30%; and room-air PaO₂ 105 is not <60 mmHg (0 each).
Total: 28 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 20 + 10 = 88.
Final answer: 88
